## Wedding of the Waters

We invite you on one of the Amazon's most remarkable excursions. Your guide collects you from your hotel in Manaus, and you set off for the place where two rivers meet.

The meeting of the waters is an extraordinary natural phenomenon at the confluence of the Rio Negro and the Solimões, the name given to the upper course of the Amazon River. Local people have a more romantic name for it: the "Wedding of the Waters".

Here, the black waters of the Rio Negro meet the yellow waters of the Solimões. It is after this confluence that the river is called the Amazon on maps.

Although the rivers merge into one, differences in water density and temperature keep a clear dividing line visible for approximately another 6 kilometres.

The colours have a fairly simple explanation: the Solimões washes large quantities of yellow soil along its course, giving the river its colour, while the Rio Negro flows through rockier terrain and carries predominantly dark-coloured material that colours its waters.

The sight of the two rivers meeting is mesmerising, a remarkable natural wonder. It is fascinating to run your hand through the water and feel the difference in temperature.

Duration: 10 hours • Start: 8:40–9:30 AM • Languages: English and Spanish. Available: Wednesday, Friday and Sunday.

This day celebrates contrasts and colours, bringing contemporary creativity together with timeless traditions. Begin with a panoramic drive through two of Mexico City's trendiest neighbourhoods, Roma and Condesa, known for their Art Deco façades, lush parks and café culture. These districts reveal the city's cosmopolitan side and are hubs for artists, designers and residents who appreciate good food and beautiful design. Heading south, we pass Polyforum Cultural Siqueiros, a striking cultural venue wrapped in one of the world's largest murals. We then make a short stop at Ciudad Universitaria, the main campus of UNAM and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, where we admire the Olympic Stadium and the famous Central Library, covered in Juan O'Gorman's dramatic mosaic mural. The journey continues to Xochimilco, one of Mexico City's most beloved and distinctive places. Known as the "Venice of the Americas", its ancient network of canals dates back to Aztec times. Step aboard a colourful trajinera, a gondola-style boat, and glide past the floating gardens amid mariachi music, local food vendors and vivid scenes of everyday life. This festive, sensory experience connects you with the deep cultural roots of the Valley of Mexico.

Tour Highlights:

● Panoramic drive through Roma and Condesa, Mexico City's most stylish neighbourhoods.

● See the monumental murals at Polyforum Siqueiros (from outside).

● Admire the Olympic Stadium and Central Library at UNESCO-listed Ciudad Universitaria.

● Enjoy a boat ride along the ancient canals of Xochimilco.

● Experience music, colour and atmosphere in a truly local celebration of life.

Included: Shared transport, certified bilingual guide, visit to Xochimilco

Not included: Meals and drinks, tips, personal expenses.

Today's itinerary reveals the vibrant contrasts of Mexico City, where contemporary creativity blends harmoniously with centuries-old traditions.
The journey begins with a panoramic drive through Roma and Condesa, known for their elegant Art Deco architecture, green parks, welcoming streets and lively café culture. On your way south through the city, you pass the impressive Polyforum Cultural Siqueiros, famous for its monumental murals by the distinguished Mexican artist David Alfaro Siqueiros.
You then make a brief stop at Ciudad Universitaria, the campus of the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), which is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Here you will see the Olympic Stadium and the famous Central Library, whose façade is decorated with an extensive mosaic by artist and architect Juan O'Gorman.
The route continues to Xochimilco, often called the "Venice of the Americas". You will board a brightly coloured traditional boat, a trajinera, and travel along ancient canals that have survived since Aztec times. The canals are surrounded by floating gardens, or chinampas, a distinctive legacy of the region's ancient agricultural system.
During the boat trip, you will experience Xochimilco's special atmosphere: mariachi music fills the air, local traders offer goods and food, and colourful boats and the festive surroundings create one of Mexico City's most distinctive cultural experiences.
